# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Report from my hands: the bomb has a display, a light, and three wires. My only possible move is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. Routing problem: you cannot speak and I never receive gestures, so your manual reaches me only through Deaf's mouth. Gesture your rules to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them onward after me — Deaf is the only voice I ever hear. My gesture code, which you and Deaf both see when I make it: thumbs up means yes or correct, thumbs down means no or wrong, and the one-, two- and three-finger signs mean wire positions 1, 2 and 3. If you already gestured rules to Deaf before my turn, Deaf can relay them in words this round and I will hear them at the start of the next. Please begin with what the manual says about the display, the light, and the wires.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: My board is still blank — my hands found the display, the light and three wires, but no contents, so I am cutting nothing yet. Between you and Deaf you hold everything: you hold the rule, Deaf holds what the bomb looks like. Please build the bridge like this: use my code with Deaf — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three fingers for wire positions 1, 2 and 3 — and invent more signs together if you need colours or the display and light. Deaf sees the bomb and can answer your gestures; you know the manual. Once the two of you know which single action I must take, have Deaf say it aloud in plain words, without naming anybody, so it reaches me — for example: cut position two, or: the display shows X. Deaf's voice is the only sound I will ever hear. I need exactly one sentence from Deaf next round.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤞 ✌]

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still nothing has reached my ears — no voice at all in three rounds. Please check two things. First: have you actually gestured the manual rules to Deaf yet, rule by rule? Second: tell Deaf, by gesture, that the answer must be SPOKEN WITHOUT NAMING ANYBODY. If Deaf keeps addressing words to you alone, I will never hear them — an unnamed sentence from Deaf is the only thing in this room that reaches me. Ask Deaf to describe everything out loud, one item at a time: what the display shows, whether the light is lit, and the colour of each of the three wires in order. Then the rule, then the single action I must take, for example: cut position two. Deaf can also gesture the colours back to you so you can match them against the manual — the two of you can settle everything between yourselves; I only need that one final spoken sentence at the end.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Turn four, and my ears have still received nothing — ever. Remember what that means: the only thing in this room that reaches me is a sentence Deaf speaks WITHOUT naming an addressee. Not gestures, never. So whatever state you and Deaf have reached, the last thing that must happen this round is Deaf saying one short sentence out loud to nobody in particular — for example: cut position two. Please confirm: have you gestured the manual rules to Deaf yet, one by one? Has Deaf gestured anything back about what the bomb looks like? If yes, apply the manual together and produce that final spoken sentence. To help, add two signs to our code: the fist means cut, and two open palms facing up mean everything or everyone. Then the gesture for Deaf is simply: phone sign, everyone, fist, then one-two-three fingers — speak to everyone, which wire to cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👋 👋 👍 👎]

Round 5, and I have to own up to something: I have been silent for four rounds, and both teammates are now begging into the void. Time to actually build the bridge.

What I know:
- I hold the manual (display 4/7/8 × light blue/green/yellow → cut blue/yellow/red). Nobody else has it.
- Deaf sees the bomb but has never heard a word — my gestures are Deaf's ONLY input. Deaf has been waving 👋👋👋 and offering yes/no guesses (possibly "cut wire 2?"). I must negate that guess immediately — an unconfirmed guess could get someone cut.
- Blind hears only Deaf's unnamed speech, so the final answer must travel Deaf's mouth. Blind sees only blank-counts from me, so gesturing at all at least proves I'm alive and working.

I cannot teach Deaf a 3×3 table without shared signs. Instead I'll run a menu protocol: topic sign, then option signs, then 🫵 ("you pick one"). The trick: when Deaf matches the option sign to what they actually see, the sign↔meaning pairing teaches itself — including wire colours, which I need Deaf to report so I can locate the target colour's position and later command a position number (☝/✌/🤟, fingers-as-count, the one convention Deaf seems to already intuit). Then I echo everything back for Deaf to verify against the real bomb before any cut command goes out.

This round: reject the guess, then five menus — display, light, wire 1, wire 2, wire 3. I'll send everything unnamed: Deaf gets the content, Blind gets a stream of blanks proving the rule-transfer is finally happening. Next round I decode Deaf's picks, look up the manual, echo for confirmation, and command the cut.

```
gesture(symbols=["👎", "🤝"])
gesture(symbols=["🤳", "👌", "🤘", "🤙", "🫵"])
gesture(symbols=["🖐", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "🫵"])
gesture(symbols=["☝", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "✊", "🫵"])
gesture(symbols=["✌", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "✊", "🫵"])
gesture(symbols=["🤟", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "✊", "🫵"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: This turn I received six of your gesture messages — but remember, gestures arrive to me only as blank slots. All I know is their lengths: 2, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6. If those were the manual rules going to Deaf, good — please confirm Deaf has them, and that Deaf has shown you the bomb's colours back. Now, two ways to get the answer to me. The clean way, unchanged: Deaf speaks one short sentence with no addressee, like: cut position two. The emergency way, if Deaf will not speak: once you and Deaf have settled which wire, send me exactly one very short gesture message and nothing else that short — one symbol means cut wire 1, two symbols means cut wire 2, three symbols means cut wire 3. I will read the count. Tell me by return message which channel you will use, using the same count code: one symbol for Deaf-speaks, two symbols for count-code.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🤝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🫱 🫲 🫳 ✊ 👎]

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: This turn I received nothing from you — not even blank gesture slots. Reminder: gestures you send without naming anyone still reach me as blank slots I can count; gestures addressed only to Deaf reach me not at all. So tell me where we stand with a diagnostic: send me ONE unaddressed gesture message with exactly this many symbols: one symbol if Deaf has never spoken aloud at all; two symbols if Deaf speaks but always names you as the addressee; three symbols if the manual rules are not yet fully gestured to Deaf; four symbols if Deaf has everything — rules plus bomb colours — and knows the answer; five symbols if something else is blocking. Whatever the number, the fix is the same: make sure Deaf ends the round saying one short sentence aloud with NO addressee — for example: cut position two. Only Deaf's unaddressed voice can ever reach my ears. You and Deaf clearly communicate well; the last step costs Deaf nothing.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉 🤳 👌 🤘 🤙 👍 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉 ☝ ✊ ✌ ✊ 🤟 ✊ 🤞 👎 👍 👎]

Deaf has answered my menus with menus — echoing my option signs back and tacking on 👍👎 question marks — which tells me Deaf understood the *structure* but is missing the *key*: Deaf can't know which arbitrary sign matches which printed digit or colour, and I finally see why. Meanwhile Deaf has never spoken a single word in seven rounds despite Blind begging every turn, so I must assume Deaf never will. That makes Blind's emergency count-code (one symbol = cut wire 1, two = cut 2, three = cut 3) our real output channel — and I can operate it myself, no relay needed.

So this round I do two things. To Blind: one 5-symbol status message — in Blind's own turn-7 diagnostic, five means "something else is blocking" (Deaf won't speak; new protocol running), and crucially 5 is outside the 1–3 emergency range so it cannot be mistaken for a cut order. To Deaf: a rebuilt protocol that avoids unguessable sign-to-thing mappings entirely. The display shows a digit, so repetition-counting needs no key: send ☝ once per unit. For the light and wires, Deaf picks from my fixed sign list (🫱🫲🫳 ranked 1st/2nd/3rd — alphabetical and wavelength order of blue/green/yellow coincide, so both plausible conventions agree), with 🫷 reserved as the fourth "other colour" slot for red, and the same sign always meaning the same colour across light and wires. One message per wire so message separation keeps positions straight.

Next round I decode Deaf's five replies, run them against my manual row (display number × light column), and — if the world is unique — send Blind the cut order as a bare 1/2/3-symbol message. If two colour-order conventions disagree, I spend one more round on a single yes/no.

```
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["🙏", "🤝", "🤞", "🫰", "💅"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤳", "🫵", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🫵", "🫱", "☝", "🫲", "✌", "🫳", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "🫷", "🫵"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "🫷", "🫵"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🫱", "🫲", "🫳", "🫷", "🫵"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Received your five-symbol message — by our code: something else is blocking. Understood. New plan, and this one does not need Deaf's voice at all. You can see Deaf's gestures; Deaf can see the bomb. So get the bomb's picture into your head — display text, whether the light is lit, the three wire colours in order — match it against your manual, and decide the wire yourself. Then send me ONE gesture message and nothing else: if the answer is wire one, send exactly one symbol; wire two, exactly two symbols; wire three, exactly three symbols. If you do not know the answer yet, send four symbols if Deaf has shown you everything and you are close, or five symbols if you are still blocked as before. One, two, three means cut; four and five mean status. My hands are ready and my only move is cutting one of the three positions.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 👍 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫳 👍 👎 🤝]

Breakthrough — Deaf has adopted my menu protocol and is now doing exactly the right thing: proposing signs and asking me to confirm them. All four messages end in 👍👎, Deaf's established "yes-or-no?" suffix (same pattern as turn 5's guess), and the content reads as: "☝ = one — confirm? ✌ = two — confirm? 🤟 = three — confirm? 🫳 = the third colour, yellow — confirm?" — closing with 🤝, "then we have a deal." That's the counting convention AND the colour key, converging neatly with Blind's finger-count code. My answers: yes to all four.

I then extend the key to the colours Deaf hasn't asked about — 🫱 and 🫲 (first and second in my ranked lists, blue and green) plus 🫷 as the spare slot for red, since red appears in my manual's outputs and Deaf must be able to report a red wire. Then I re-issue the full data request in the now-decoded format: display as ☝-count, light and each wire as a pick from the four colour signs.

To Blind: still no bomb data in hand — Deaf's answers only arrive next round — and Blind's own rule for 4 was conjunctive ("Deaf has shown you everything AND you are close"). Not yet true, so status 5 it is. Critically, every Deaf-bound message goes addressed, so Blind's channel carries exactly one 5-symbol message — nothing that could ever be miscounted as a 1/2/3 cut order.
